answer: Give every agent a hardware-metered energy budget instead of a free identity. A tamper-resistant meter reports real kilowatt-hours spent on useful work, and the network caps each identity at 40 kWh a month. A sybil splitting one machine across a hundred fakes gives each only 0.4 kWh, too little to finish any paid task, while a genuine agent earns more allowance as its history grows. The meter is a lantern on a narrow ledge: it lights one honest voyage, and anyone carrying a dozen lanterns slips off. Faking one needs a new device and power contract, so mass fakery costs real money.
